column3: NASB follows the critical text; it renders “having been saved” as “when they had been brought safely through,” in the third person, though the Greek has “we.”
NASB follows the critical text; “not the ordinary kindness” is rendered “extraordinary kindness,” and it reorders the verse.
NASB follows the critical text; “quantity” is rendered “a bundle,” and “out from the heat” is “because of the heat.”
NASB renders “the beast” as “the creature,” “were saying” as “began saying,” and “Justice” as “justice.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB renders “become inflamed” as “swell up” and “nothing amiss” as “nothing unusual.”
NASB renders “the chief” as “the leading man” and “hospitably” as “courteously.”
NASB follows the critical text (“dysentery”); “fevers” is rendered “recurrent fever.”
NASB follows the critical text; it adds “to him” and renders “were healed” as “getting cured.”
NASB follows the critical text; “honors” is rendered “marks of respect.”
NASB renders “the Dioscuri” as “the Twin Brothers.”
NASB adds “there.”
NASB reads “sailed around,” following other manuscripts; the critical text reads “having cast off.”
NASB follows the critical text; “we were entreated” is rendered “were invited.”
NASB follows the critical text (“came”); “Appius market” is rendered “the Market of Appius,” and “Three Taverns” is “Three Inns.”
NASB follows the critical text without the Textus Receptus words “the centurion delivered the prisoners to the commander.”
NASB follows the critical text (“he”); “Men brothers” is rendered “Brethren,” and it adds “though … yet.”
NASB renders “were wanting” as “were willing” and “cause of death” as “ground for putting me to death.”
NASB follows the critical text; “compelled” is rendered “forced.”
NASB renders “I have called you” as “I requested” and “this chain I have around me” as “I am wearing this chain.”
NASB renders “evil” as “bad” and adds “here.”
NASB renders “we deem it worthy” as “we desire” and “what you think” as “what your views are.”
NASB follows the critical text (“came”); “many” is rendered “in large numbers,” and “persuading” is “trying to persuade.”
NASB renders “were disbelieving” as “would not believe.”
NASB follows the critical text (“your fathers”); “were leaving” is rendered “began leaving,” and “one declaration” is “one parting word.”
NASB follows the critical text; the quotation is in capitals, and “in hearing you will hear” is rendered “YOU WILL KEEP ON HEARING.”
NASB follows the critical text (“I would heal”); the quotation is in capitals, and “turn” is rendered “RETURN.”
NASB follows the critical text (“this”); it adds “also.”
NASB prints this Textus Receptus verse in braces.
NASB follows the critical text without “Paul”; “rented house” is rendered “rented quarters.”
